messages:
Maria: Heads up - after rolling kernel 6.1.14 -> 6.1.16 in eu-west-1 we started seeing repeated NCCL timeouts on p4 instances, plus a spike in kernel OOMs on a subset of nodes.
Alert-Bot: [ALERT] 1825123456 GPU-fleet: NCCL errors > threshold in eu-west-1. Top hosts: gpu-ew-12,gpu-ew-15,gpu-ew-22
Kevin: @Maria can you paste last 10 lines of dmesg from gpu-ew-12? also any driver logs (nvidia-smi -q) would help.
Maria: dmesg snippet:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0000:03:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.570123] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4123 (python) score 987
[ 1234.572345] nv_peer_mem: version mismatch
```
Maria: nvidia-smi shows some GPUs reporting ECC errors, some processes stuck in D state.
Jonathan: sounds like a kernel-driver ABI mismatch surfaced under certain driver+cuda combinations. Did we also update CUDA libs in the same maintenance window?
Maria: only kernel and microcode. Driver (535.xx) stayed pinned. But the kernel upgrade introduced a subtle change in pci hotplug behavior.
Tara: short-term: we should roll back the kernel for the affected pool and pin the package. Long-term: need a lockstep compatibility matrix to prevent this slip.
Kevin: Agreed. Plan proposal:
  1) Cordon + drain affected nodes in eu-west-1 (gpu-ew-*)
  2) Reboot into previous kernel (6.1.14) where available or reinstall and mark hold
  3) Run NCCL smoke tests across 4-node allreduce
  4) Open incident and notify Dedicated customers in that region
  5) Add kernel-driver gate to rollout pipeline
Maria: ops commands I'm running:
```
# mark hold on debian hosts
sudo apt-get install linux-image-6.1.14 linux-headers-6.1.14
sudo apt-mark hold linux-image-6.1.14 linux-headers-6.1.14
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon gpu-ew-12
kubectl drain gpu-ew-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Jonathan: note: apt-mark hold only prevents upgrades, doesn't prevent accidental package removal during reprovision. We should also pin in our image build (packer) and add a lock file in infra repo.
Ops-Oncall: @Maria started drain on gpu-ew-12,15,22. Reboots triggered. Reprovision fallback in progress for hosts not booting back.
Deploy-Bot: Code deploy paused for kernel updates in eu-west-1 (lock acquired by eng-infra).
Kevin: For rpm systems, we should use dnf versionlock plugin. Add explicit entries to /etc/dnf/plugins/versionlock.list like:
```
kernel-core-6.1.14-1.el8
kernel-modules-6.1.14-1.el8
```
Tara: Cost/ops tradeoff note: holding older kernels for a long time increases attack surface / maintenance burden. But flipping kernels across fleets causes churn and scheduling disruptions — customer impact > infra toil for short-term.
Maria: Immediate mitigation results: nodes rebooted into 6.1.14, NCCL errors dropped to baseline on those nodes. Still seeing degraded I/O on two hosts which are mid-reprovision; isolating them.
Jonathan: Can we add a temporary model: kernel holds per image-family and a QR (quick rollback) label on node objects so we can trace which nodes need manual intervention later? Also add a 'compat_version' tag on GPU nodes.
Kevin: Yes — plan to update node labels: gpu.kernel_version and gpu.driver_version. Rollout tooling will consult these before upgrading kernel on that node pool.
Maria: Quick checklist for post-incident:
- [x] rollback eu-west-1 affected nodes
- [x] pin kernel packages on image and runtime
- [ ] add pre-rollout NCCL allreduce test harness
- [ ] author lockstep matrix mapping kernel <-> driver <-> cuda <-> microcode
- [ ] add automated gating to canary pipeline
- [ ] run cost analysis for holding old kernels long-term
Jonathan: For the matrix: we should include firmware (BIOS/microcode) because we saw pci hotplug differences. Also flag known-good combos and also allowed-fallback combos (e.g., nvidia driver X will accept kernel Y but with known perf regression).
Ops-Oncall: Customer comms drafted for Dedicated customers in eu-west-1. SRE lead to review.
Kevin: One more operational quirk — we noticed NCCL fell back to socket transport on some failing hosts. That increased network egress and hit our VPC NATs; egress cost bump ~+12% for that window. Add cost alert per-probe.
Tara: Actionable infra changes:
  - infra/images: pin kernel package versions, bake new images with old kernel where needed
  - infra/ansible: add module to manage versionlocks across distros
  - infra/ci: add nightly compatibility matrix validation (small cluster allreduce/run perf)
  - console: surface 'compat_status' in node details (driver/kernel/cuda)
Maria: Additional note: for future hotfixes we should have a 'pin & live-test' path: temporarily pin kernel on 5% of capacity and run load-test for 2 hours before global roll.
Jonathan: Agreed. Also add a preflight that runs a 4-node NCCL allreduce and a CUDA sanity check inside the canary stage. Fail rollout on regression > 5% latency.
Ops-Oncall: tagging this thread for postmortem: incident-1825123456
SRE-Bot: Postmortem recipe checklist created: /incidents/1825123456/checklist.md
Maria: thanks all. I'll follow up with PR to infra repo for versionlock + labels. Please add any missing tasks to the incident board. :thumbsup:
Kevin: ack. Good catch, Maria. Let's also schedule an RFC to formalize lockstep matrix and gating policy next week.
